note: Sizing rules that turn a town's flow deficit into units to build. CITED = taken from the named source. ASSUMPTION = no source checked; a working figure the user should replace. Every value can be changed in the page.

rules.label: Years between emptyings of a tank or pit
rules.source: Balasubramanya et al. 2017, PLoS ONE 12(3): e0171735. Pit latrines in Bhaluka, Bangladesh, need emptying about once every 3 to 4 years.
rules.caveat: Measured on rural pit latrines. Town septic tanks may fill at a different rate.

rules.label: Sludge removed at one emptying
rules.source: Vacuum tugs in service in Bangladeshi towns hold 0.6 m³ (Mark 1) or 2 m³ (Mark 2): study of mechanical emptying services in Dhaka, Faridpur and Khulna (copy held by sswm.info). Vacuum trucks elsewhere hold 3 to 12 m³ (Tilley et al. 2014, Compendium of Sanitation Systems and Technologies).
rules.caveat: Assumes one vehicle load per emptying.

rules.label: Emptying trips one vehicle makes in a day
rules.source: No source checked. Depends on haul distance to the treatment site.

rules.label: Dry solids in the sludge delivered
rules.source: No single source: published values range widely (about 5 kg/m³ of raw sludge received at Cambérène, Dakar, in Sandec News 10, 2009). Measure it locally before design.
rules.caveat: Drying-bed area is directly proportional to this figure.

rules.label: Solids an unplanted drying bed can take
rules.unit: kg of dry solids per m² per year
rules.source: Dodane and Ronteltap 2014, Unplanted drying beds, chapter 7 of Faecal Sludge Management: Systems Approach for Implementation and Operation (IWA Publishing): 100 to 200 in tropical climates, 100 for poorer conditions and 200 for optimal.

rules.label: Waste one collection van moves in a day
rules.source: No source checked. Payload times trips a day; use the municipality's own vehicle records.

rules.label: Share of collected organic waste that reaches the compost plant sorted
rules.source: No source checked. Depends on separation at source.

rules.label: Organic waste one compost plant module takes
rules.source: Waste Concern, Dhaka: small-scale plants take up to 3 tonnes a day, medium-scale 3 to 10 (Sinha 2010, presentation to the UN Commission on Sustainable Development intersessional meeting).

rules.label: Compost from one tonne of organic waste
rules.source: Waste Concern, Dhaka: a quarter of a tonne of compost from one tonne of organic waste (Sinha 2010, as above).

rules.label: Wastewater per person reaching a shared treatment unit
rules.source: No source checked. Use the town's water supply figure.
rules.caveat: Only used where groundwater is high and soak pits will not work.
